headline: High: shared MCP/API surfaces create prompt-injection and data-flow risks; medium leakage/conflict from overlapping file and network behaviors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and stdin/stdout, so it may ingest external content through shared channels; plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and broad egress, so its outputs can be routed into OpenBB workflows. No direct bridge is documented, so this is inferred from documented surfaces rather than observed interaction.
conditions: IF plano outputs are copied into an OpenBB MCP session or stdin/stdout pipeline
IF OpenBBTerminal treats file or API content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted content
Add a provenance tag to all plano outputs before ingestion
Require manual review of any text that becomes an OpenBB command
Use a separate workspace for each agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while plano handles logs, traces, metrics, and agentic signals with broad egress. If they share a workspace or config path, sensitive financial material can flow into plano’s outbound requests or logs. The pairwise leak is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same directory or config bundle
IF plano forwards request context or logs containing OpenBB data to a remote backend
mitigations: Separate workspaces and config files
Redact financial fields before any plano request
Turn off verbose logging for shared sessions
Restrict plano egress to approved endpoints

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances and can write through Python environments, while plano does not support multiple instances and uses an out-of-process dataplane. That creates a realistic coordination risk if both target the same mutable config or shared resource, though no direct lock mechanism is documented. I choose medium because the overlap is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same config.yaml or shared runtime state
IF OpenBBTerminal and plano are run concurrently against one mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate config files per agent
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist
Make shared resources read-only during analysis
Snapshot configs before starting either agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs and MCP outputs, and plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. If plano’s generated text is treated as authoritative by OpenBBTerminal, errors can cascade into downstream financial analysis or actions. There is no documented verification barrier between them, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses plano output as a source of facts or commands
IF no human verification step occurs before OpenBB acts on plano text
mitigations: Require a human approval step before acting on plano output
Mark plano output as untrusted in prompts
Cross-check critical facts against a second source
Limit plano to drafting, not execution

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while plano’s documented data classes are logs, traces, metrics, and agentic signals. If the same regulated dataset is routed through both, retention or residency mismatches can arise. Only OpenBB’s compliance-relevant data classes are explicit, so I cite it directly and note plano’s side as the logging sink.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is sent through plano logging or tracing
IF retention settings differ between OpenBBTerminal and plano for the same dataset
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from logs and traces
Set matching retention windows for both systems
Review secret handling in OpenBBTerminal before deployment
Keep compliance-sensitive workloads on a separate path
